claude.country: Spain, Denmark, Egypt, Algeria, Uganda, Ghana, Malawi
claude.sample_unit: patients (1792 Spain, 1008 Denmark, 25 per African centre)

links.outcome: AUC of model fine-tuned on small local African samples versus trained from scratch
links.effect: Fine-tuning raised AUC to 99.2%, 98.8%, 99.8% (Malawi, Egypt, Algeria) versus 93.3%, 90.8%, 90.3% from scratch; maximum AUC reached with about 4-6 local patients.
links.quote: For example, in the case of Malawi, Egypt and Algeria, the maximum average AUC when training from scratch is 93.3%, 90.8% and 90.3%, respectively, while transfer learning increases the average performance to 99.2%, 98.8% and 99.8%.

links.outcome: Performance of Spanish-trained model on African low-resource centres versus Danish high-resource centre
links.effect: Danish AUC >95% with n>500; African centres showed inconsistent and lower performance, especially with scarce training samples; single-centre model did not reach desired performance.
links.quote: Although the Spanish model has a good generalisation ability in another European dataset, the African clinical centres with low-resource settings manifest an inconsistent pattern and lower performance, especially when the number of training samples is scarce.

links.outcome: Performance variation across sites and scanner devices
links.effect: Performance varied across five African centres with different scanners; Algeria with similar protocol reached AUC 97.9 ± 1.9% with over 1000 training samples, others lower and inconsistent.
links.quote: In the case where the images are acquired using a similar protocol to that of the European datasets, such as Algeria (Table 1 ), the model shows a competitive performance (average AUC of 97.9 ± 1.9 %) when more than 1000 samples are used for training.

links.outcome: Generalisation of model to new population/context (low-resource African centres)
links.effect: Single-centre model trained in Spain did not reach desired performance in Malawi, Egypt, Algeria, Uganda or Ghana.
links.quote: Our results showed that a model trained using a single-centre approach did not reach the desired performance when applied to a new centre in low-resource settings acquired in Malawi, Egypt, Algeria, Uganda or Ghana.

openai.country: Spain; Denmark; Malawi; Egypt; Uganda; Ghana; Algeria

links.effect: Denmark average AUC >95% when n>500; African low-resource centres had inconsistent/lower performance; Algeria 97.9 ± 1.9% when protocol was similar.
links.quote: Although the Spanish model has a good generalisation ability in another European dataset, the African clinical centres with low-resource settings manifest an inconsistent pattern and lower performance, especially when the number of training samples is scarce.

links.effect: Single-centre Spanish model did not reach desired performance in Malawi, Egypt, Algeria, Uganda or Ghana; Denmark AUC was >95% when n>500.
links.quote: Our results showed that a model trained using a single-centre approach did not reach the desired performance when applied to a new centre in low-resource settings acquired in Malawi, Egypt, Algeria, Uganda or Ghana.

links.effect: Training from scratch AUC 93.3%, 90.8%, 90.3% in Malawi, Egypt, Algeria; transfer learning improved to 99.2%, 98.8%, 99.8%.
links.quote: For example, in the case of Malawi, Egypt and Algeria, the maximum average AUC when training from scratch is 93.3%, 90.8% and 90.3%, respectively, while transfer learning increases the average performance to 99.2%, 98.8% and 99.8%.

links.effect: Baseline performance differed by African site: Malawi 93.3%, Egypt 90.8%, Algeria 90.3%, while Uganda and Ghana were 99.5% and 97.6%.
links.quote: In Uganda and Ghana, the improvement given by transfer learning is smaller since the maximum baseline performance is already high: 99.5% and 97.6% versus 100% and 98.6% with fine-tuning, respectively.

gemini.country: Spain, Denmark, Egypt, Algeria, Uganda, Ghana, Malawi

links.outcome: cross-site generalisation of fetal plane classifier
links.effect: Spanish model achieved >95% AUC in Denmark but exhibited inconsistent patterns and lower performance across low-resource African centres.
links.quote: Although the Spanish model has a good generalisation ability in another European dataset, the African clinical centres with low-resource settings manifest an inconsistent pattern and lower performance, especially when the number of training samples is scarce.

links.outcome: fetal plane classification AUC with local transfer learning
links.effect: Transfer learning increased average AUC from 93.3%, 90.8%, and 90.3% (training from scratch) to 99.2%, 98.8%, and 99.8% in Malawi, Egypt, and Algeria, respectively.
links.quote: For example, in the case of Malawi, Egypt and Algeria, the maximum average AUC when training from scratch is 93.3%, 90.8% and 90.3%, respectively, while transfer learning increases the average performance to 99.2%, 98.8% and 99.8%.

screen.practice: local recalibration via transfer learning before deployment at new site
screen.reason: Evaluates transfer learning / domain adaptation strategies as a practice to mitigate domain-shift and restore model performance when deploying ultrasound AI models to low-resource African clinical settings.
